usage.note: One judging pass; the two comparison rungs reused the checkpoints (0 new calls). Fitting is free.

H1_macro_f1_objective.note: macro_f1 selection LOWERED partial F1 (0.30 vs 0.40) and macro F1 (0.50 vs 0.52) versus the existing accuracy_guarded_partial, which already prefers partial F1 within an accuracy band. Pure macro_f1 relaxed the lower cutpoint (75->50) without better partial separation.

H2_two_gate.note: Two independent cutpoints (presence on change_evidence, completeness on specification_fidelity) did NOT separate partial better. two_gate raised balanced accuracy to 0.622 by lifting minority recall, but at a large precision cost (no->partial 28, no->yes 31 out of 289 no cases), so partial F1 fell to 0.238 and accuracy to 0.727.

advancement_gate: FAILED — two_gate did not beat both min_scalar rungs on partial F1 and macro F1. Per the preregistered stopping rule, region grounding (step 3) is NOT auto-advanced.
interpretation: The best calibrator on this dev slice is the EXISTING min-scalar + accuracy-guarded-partial (partial F1 0.40, macro F1 0.52). Neither a macro-F1 objective nor two independent cutpoints improves partial. This is strong evidence that partial is a SIGNAL problem, not a calibration-representation problem: the model's change_evidence/specification_fidelity scores do not cleanly encode completeness, so no cutpoint reshuffling separates partial. Note also that the flat scored path already achieves partial F1 ~0.40 here — the partial-F1=0.0 collapse seen earlier was specific to the delta-tree's free-form labels + coverage objective, not the flat path.

stronger_judge_ab.gate: does gpt-4.1 raise partial F1 above the gpt-4.1-mini best (0.405)? — FAILED (0.315 < 0.405)
stronger_judge_ab.note: A stronger judge (gpt-4.1) on the same inputs did NOT move partial — it regressed partial F1, accuracy, and macro F1 vs gpt-4.1-mini. Consistent with the earlier EditInspector gpt-4.1 A/B. Three independent negatives (two-gate, macro-F1 objective, stronger judge) triangulate that partial is not fixable by calibration or a bigger LLM on source+edited images + instruction alone.

next: Calibration and judge-model levers are exhausted. The only untried lever is a genuinely different signal (step 3: region-grounded completeness — pixel-change localization independent of the judge's semantic read). Its upside is bounded (~+7 accuracy points) and further capped by partial label noise (only 8-31% of partial targets are unanimous). Proceeding is a deliberate research bet, not an automatic step.
